cards.back: Advanced Persistent Threat: targeted, long-term, well-funded campaign combining multiple vectors. A campaign, not a single malware.
Email, SMS, RCS, instant messaging, and collaboration tools: phishing, smishing, links, and attachments.
Rich Communication Services: successor to SMS, enriched phishing vector — exam objective concept.
QR code phishing: the code hides the malicious URL. Classified as image-based.
Content embedded in an image, fake CAPTCHA, deepfake — exam objective concepts.
Embedded macros, RTF and PDF documents: code execution or links exploiting an unpatched reader.
Extensions, JavaScript, password managers, cookies, and session tokens.
Stolen cookies / session tokens: the attacker takes over a valid session without password or MFA.
Compromised infrastructure and virtualized devices, stolen session keys.
Remote desktop (RDP), VNC, VPN: remote access with weak credentials or misconfiguration.
Mobile devices, workstations, servers, tablets, trusted devices, native tools, and living-off-the-land.
Using system tools (PowerShell, WMI) to operate without dropping malware: detected by behavior.
Third-party providers, MSPs, logistics providers, and SaaS: compromising a trusted third party.
Malicious USB: autorun, keylogger, or data theft on a workstation.
Impersonation, contractor, visitor, spoofed biometrics, watering hole.
Cameras, sensors, printers: connected devices that are often unmanaged and unpatched.
Industrial OT / SCADA; physical = lock and key, access control vestibule, badges (tailgating).
Bluetooth, radio frequency (RF), and NFC: proximity wireless vectors.
